newsitem.title: USA: Tax-advantaged preferreds, US corp issuance brisk.
newsitem.headline: Tax-advantaged preferreds, US corp issuance brisk.

text.p: Issuance of tax-advantaged preferred securities held up its torrid pace on Tuesday and complemented almost $1.0 billion of new high-grade U.S. corporate bond debt, dealers said.

Spreads of the "new" preferred securities posted less impressive tightening when freed than seen during the past week, however, the debt restrained by brisk selling and prospects for another $10 billion this year alone.
Topping the slate of "new" preferreds on Tuesday, JPM Capital Trust I issued $750 million in capital securities due July 15, 2027 via lead underwriter JP Morgan Securities Inc.
The 7.54 percent Aa2/AA-minus rated capital securities were priced at par to yield a spread of 104 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, the underwriter said.
The initial size of the deal was expected to come in at about $600 million but was increased to $750 million to meet investor demand, sources said.

Spreads for the preferreds had tightened early in the session but made little headway into the afternoon session, traders said. Reports of heavy selling of fresh issuance by several accounts sapped some of the enthusiasm and led to lackluster activity at the close.
"You always have certain accounts that will do that but this was very early," one syndicate source said. "Once this paper was placed some people thought that would be it."
On the flip side, spreads of bank and finance corporate debt issues began to stabilize after taking a week's worth of hits in connection to the issuance of the "new" preferreds.

Meanwhile, the National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) on Tuesday recommended that insurance companies treat trust preferred stock as debt for risk-based capital purposes. The NAIC ruling should increase insurance companies' investments in the securities, analysts said.
Turning to straight corporate debt, prices were little changed in sympathy with U.S. Treasuries but issuers spiced up the primary with about $1.0 billion in fresh paper.
Investment grade issuance included the following deals:
--ABN AMRO Bank NV's Chicago branch issued $400 million in Aa2/AA rated subordinated debt due 2026 as 7.30s to yield xx via leads ABN AMRO and Salomon Brothers.

--Norwest Corp issued $200 million Aa3/AA-minus rated 10-year non-calleble notes at par to yield 6.55 percent, or 45.6 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries through a Lehman Brothers syndicate.

--Highwoods/Forsyth LP issued $210 million debt in two parts via Goldman Sachs. The first tranche of $100 million seven-year debt was priced as 6-3/4s to yield 6.79 percent or 80 basis points over Treasuries and another $110 million 10-year notes priced as 7s to yield 7.038 percent or 95 basis points over the curve.
In the high-yield market, market participants reported mostly quiet activity ahead of the Thanksgiving Day holiday with exception to some new issue offerings.
--AmerKing Inc issued $100 million 10-year B3/B-minus rated senior notes at par to yield 10.75 percent via Donaldson, Lufin & Jenrette Securities.
--Radnor Holdings Inc issued $100 million B2/single-B seven-year senior notes at par to yield 10 percent or 398 basis points over Treasuries via Alex Brown & Sons.
--Chevy Chase Bank set $100 million B1/B-plus 12-year subordinated debentures at par to yield 9.25 percent or 314 basis points over Treasuries via Merrill Lynch & Co Inc.
PSA The Bond Market Trade Association has recommended an early 1400 EST/1900 GMT close for the U.S. Treasury and related debt markets on Wednesday and Friday.
